stories.headline: US strikes near Strait of Hormuz; Iran calls it 'gross violation' as Brent tops $99

key_facts.fact: US Central Command said it carried out 'self-defence' strikes on Iranian missile sites and boats attempting to lay mines in southern Iran (Hormozgan province) on Monday, with explosions heard early Tuesday May 26
key_facts.excerpt: The US Central Command (Centcom) said Iranian missile sites and boats attempting to place mines had been targeted with what it called 'self-defence strikes' in southern Iran on Monday.

key_facts.fact: Iran's foreign ministry called the strikes a 'gross violation' of the ceasefire that has held since April 8 and said it held the US responsible for the consequences
key_facts.excerpt: Iran's foreign ministry said US strikes in Iran's southern Hormozgan province, where Iranian media reported sounds of explosions early on Tuesday, represented a 'gross violation' of a tenuous ceasefire in place for nearly seven weeks.

key_facts.fact: Global benchmark Brent crude rose about 3.5% on Tuesday May 26 to more than $99 a barrel following news of the US strikes
key_facts.excerpt: Global benchmark Brent crude oil rose about 3.5% on Tuesday to more than $99 a barrel following news of the US strikes.

key_facts.fact: A high-level Iranian delegation including Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf and Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati was in Doha, Qatar for talks aimed at ending the war
key_facts.excerpt: Top Iranian negotiators have travelled to Qatar... Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, and Central Bank Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati are part of the delegation visiting Doha.

key_facts.fact: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, speaking in Jaipur, India, said negotiating a deal could 'take a few days' and stressed the Strait of Hormuz would remain open 'one way or the other'
key_facts.excerpt: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said negotiating a deal to halt the conflict could 'take a few days.'

key_facts.fact: China urged the parties to fulfil their ceasefire commitments and resolve disputes peacefully, with spokeswoman Mao Ning expressing concern
key_facts.excerpt: China, Washington's great power rival and a major energy importer, expressed concern. 'We urge the parties concerned to fulfil their ceasefire commitments, resolve disputes through peaceful means... and promote the early restoration of peace,' foreign ministry spokeswoman Mao Ning told reporters.

key_facts.fact: The war began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran on February 28; Iran has effectively blocked the Strait of Hormuz, through which around one fifth of the world's oil passes
key_facts.excerpt: Iran has effectively blocked the vital shipping lane, through which around one fifth of the world's oil passes, since the US and Israel started the conflict on 28 February.

sources.title: US strikes were 'gross violation' of ceasefire, Iran says
Iran says new US strikes violate ceasefire; oil rises again

stories.headline: Israeli strikes kill 31 in south Lebanon as troops push past Yellow Line into Hezbollah area

key_facts.fact: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed 31 people on Tuesday May 26, including at least four children and three women, with 40 wounded, the Lebanese health ministry said
key_facts.excerpt: Israeli strikes on southern Lebanon killed 31 people on Tuesday, the Lebanese health ministry said... the health ministry said 31 people, including at least four children and three women, were killed in attacks and 40 wounded.

key_facts.fact: Israel's military said it struck more than 100 Hezbollah sites across southern Lebanon and the eastern Bekaa Valley overnight, hitting storage facilities, command centers and observation points
key_facts.excerpt: Israel's military said it struck more than 100 Hezbollah sites across southern Lebanon and the eastern Bekaa Valley area overnight, adding that it targeted storage facilities, command centers and observation points.

key_facts.fact: An Israeli military official told AFP that troops had begun operating beyond the Israel-declared 'Yellow Line,' which runs around 10 kilometres deep into Lebanese territory, expanding ground operations
key_facts.excerpt: An Israeli military official told AFP that troops had begun operating beyond the Israel-announced 'Yellow Line' in south Lebanon, which runs around 10 kilometres (six miles) deep inside Lebanese territory.

key_facts.fact: Hezbollah said it confronted Israeli troops advancing on the town of Zawtar al-Sharqiyah, overlooking Nabatieh, using explosive drones, rockets and artillery
key_facts.excerpt: Hezbollah said on Tuesday it had targeted Israeli forces advancing toward the southern Lebanese town of Zawtar al-Sharqiya with explosive drones, rockets and artillery.

key_facts.fact: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Tuesday his country was intensifying operations in Lebanon to reinforce a security buffer zone protecting northern Israeli communities
key_facts.excerpt: Netanyahu on Tuesday said his country was intensifying operations in Lebanon... 'We are reinforcing the security buffer zone in order to protect communities of northern Israel,' he added.

key_facts.fact: Several strikes hit near the Qaraoun Dam on the Litani river; the Litani River Authority warned that targeting it could lead to 'catastrophic risks' for downstream residents and infrastructure
key_facts.excerpt: Several strikes also hit near Lebanon's largest dam in the Litani river's Qaraoun lake in the east. The Litani River Authority issued a statement warning that 'any direct or indirect targeting of the Qaraoun Dam or its facilities could lead to catastrophic risks for residents, infrastructure, and vital installations.'

key_facts.fact: The cumulative toll from the Israeli offensive since the war began on March 2 had reached 3,213 dead and 9,737 wounded by May 26, per the Lebanese health ministry; the escalation comes days ahead of Lebanese-Israeli talks in Washington
key_facts.excerpt: Lebanon's health ministry says the cumulative toll from the Israeli offensive since March 2 had reached 3,213 dead and 9,737 wounded by May 26.

sources.title: Israeli strikes kill 31 in south Lebanon as Israel expands ground operations
Israel and Hezbollah clash along strategic river after overnight strikes across Lebanon

stories.headline: NASA awards nearly $1B in Moon Base contracts, names Blue Origin, Astrolab, Lunar Outpost

key_facts.fact: NASA announced the first phase of its Moon Base program on Tuesday May 26 at agency headquarters in Washington, awarding nearly $1 billion in contracts to commercial partners for rovers, cargo landers and robotic drones
key_facts.excerpt: Nasa has officially laid out the first phase of an ambitious Moon Base program... awarding nearly $1 billion in contracts to commercial partners for rovers, cargo landers and robotic drones. The plan, announced Tuesday at NASA headquarters...

key_facts.fact: Astrolab received roughly $219 million and Lunar Outpost about $220 million to develop crewed and autonomous lunar terrain vehicles, while Blue Origin secured a separate contract worth about $188 million to transport the rovers to the Moon
key_facts.excerpt: Astrolab received roughly $219 million and Lunar Outpost about $220 million to develop crewed and autonomous lunar terrain vehicles, while Blue Origin secured a separate contract worth approximately $188 million to transport the rovers to the Moon.

key_facts.fact: NASA announced the first three missions, Moon Base I, II and III, targeted to launch by the end of 2026 with uncrewed landers, the first of more than a dozen Moon Base missions planned for announcement this year
key_facts.excerpt: During the event, NASA announced the first three Moon Base missions... NASA said the missions represent the first of more than a dozen Moon Base missions the agency plans to announce this year.

key_facts.fact: Moon Base I, targeted for no earlier than fall 2026, will use Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 'Endurance' lander to deliver payloads to the Shackleton Connecting Ridge region of the lunar South Pole
key_facts.excerpt: Moon Base I is targeted for launch no earlier than fall 2026 and will use Blue Origin's Blue Moon Mark 1 Endurance lander to deliver NASA payloads to the Shackleton Connecting Ridge region.

key_facts.fact: NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency is shifting from isolated demonstration missions toward 'repeatable operations,' aiming for a sustained human presence near the lunar South Pole by the early 2030s
key_facts.excerpt: Nasa Administrator Jared Isaacman said the agency is shifting from isolated demonstration missions toward 'repeatable operations' built around commercial logistics and surface mobility systems.

key_facts.fact: Other Phase 1 missions involve Astrobotic's Griffin lander (carrying Astrolab's FLIP rover and over 1,100 pounds of cargo) and Intuitive Machines' Nova-C Trinity lander
key_facts.excerpt: Moon Base II... will use Astrobotic's Griffin lander and will transport more than 1,100 pounds of cargo, including Astrolab's FLIP rover. Moon Base III... will use Intuitive Machines' Nova-C Trinity lunar lander.

sources.title: Unveiled: $1 billion NASA contract for moon base rovers and landers
NASA Awards Moon Base Contracts to 4 Companies

stories.headline: Samsung union approves deal with ~$340K average chip-worker bonus, averting strike

key_facts.fact: Samsung Electronics' largest union voted in favor of a compensation deal that will hand chip workers an average bonus of about $340,000, staving off a strike that threatened to disrupt global chip supply
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics Co.'s largest union voted in favor of a compensation deal that will hand chip workers an average bonus of about $340,000, staving off a strike that threatened to disrupt global chip supply.

key_facts.fact: The vote, which concluded Wednesday May 27 after five months of negotiations, passed with 73.7% (46,142 of 62,616 ballots cast) in favor, on a 95.5% turnout of 65,593 eligible voters
key_facts.excerpt: Samsung Electronics and its unions concluded five grueling months of wage negotiations after workers voted to ratify a tentative agreement on Wednesday... 62,616 of 65,593 eligible voters cast ballots, a turnout of 95.5 percent, with 73.7 percent, or 46,142 members, voting in favor.

key_facts.fact: The deal allocates 10.5% of the semiconductor (DS) division's operating profit as stock-based bonuses plus an additional 1.5% in cash, running for 10 years contingent on aggressive profit targets
key_facts.excerpt: The government-mediated agreement... allocates 10.5% of Samsung's semiconductor division operating profit as stock-based bonuses, plus an additional 1.5% in cash. The program runs for 10 years, contingent on the division hitting aggressive annual operating profit targets.

key_facts.fact: Memory chip employees are projected to receive roughly $400,000 each while colleagues in smartphones and home appliances receive closer to about $4,000, exposing deep divisions among workers
key_facts.excerpt: a package that will pay memory chip employees roughly $400,000 each this year while their colleagues in smartphones and home appliances receive closer to just $4,000.

key_facts.fact: On Tuesday May 26 the Suwon District Court dismissed an injunction filed by five workers from Samsung's Device eXperience (DX) division seeking to block the vote, clearing the way for ratification
key_facts.excerpt: The Suwon District Court rejected the injunction filed by five employees from Samsung's Device eXperience (DX) division, who had argued it was unfairly excluded from the vote.

key_facts.fact: The agreement averts a planned 18-day general strike by 48,000 workers that would have risked disrupting global AI chip supply chains
key_facts.excerpt: The government-mediated agreement, struck last week to avert an 18-day general strike by 48,000 workers...

sources.title: Samsung Union Votes in Favor of Deal, Averting Chip Plant Strike
Samsung's wage deal sealed but exposes deep divisions among workers, shareholders
Samsung $400,000 worker bonuses near approval after clearing legal challenge

stories.headline: OpenRouter raises $113M Series B led by CapitalG at $1.3B valuation as token volume hits 25T/week

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter, the AI model exchange, announced Tuesday May 26 a $113 million Series B led by Alphabet's growth fund CapitalG, with participation from NVentures (NVIDIA), ServiceNow Ventures, MongoDB Ventures, Snowflake Ventures, Databricks Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz and Menlo Ventures
key_facts.excerpt: OpenRouter... announced Tuesday it has raised a $113 million Series B led by CapitalG, Alphabet's independent growth fund. The round included participation from NVentures, NVIDIA's venture arm, alongside ServiceNow Ventures, MongoDB Ventures, Snowflake Ventures, Databricks Ventures, Andreessen Horowitz, and Menlo Ventures.

key_facts.fact: Menlo Ventures said the round was raised at a $1.3 billion valuation, and that OpenRouter's revenue has already doubled since the round closed in February
key_facts.excerpt: they've raised a $113M Series B at a $1.3B valuation led by CapitalG. Their revenue has already doubled since the round was done in February.

key_facts.fact: OpenRouter's traffic has climbed to 25 trillion tokens per week (roughly 100 trillion per month), a 5x increase from six months ago, and it now serves more than 8 million users
key_facts.excerpt: OpenRouter said its traffic has climbed to 25 trillion tokens per week, or roughly 100 trillion tokens per month, marking a 5x increase from six months ago... The platform says it now serves more than 8 million users globally.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2023, OpenRouter provides developers and enterprises access to more than 400 AI models (from providers including Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, xAI and DeepSeek) via a single API, routing requests and managing failover to reduce vendor lock-in
key_facts.excerpt: OpenRouter's infrastructure manages and optimizes inference across more than 400 models from AI providers including Anthropic, Google, OpenAI, xAI, and DeepSeek. The platform serves over 8 million global users.

key_facts.fact: The raise comes a year after OpenRouter's $40 million seed and Series A; CEO Alex Atallah said success now depends on continuously routing across a changing market rather than picking a single model
key_facts.excerpt: 'Running inference at scale is fundamentally a multi-model problem. The era of picking a single model is over,' said Alex Atallah, CEO and co-founder of OpenRouter.

sources.title: OpenRouter raises $113M as AI token usage surges to 100 trillion monthly
OpenRouter Now Processes More Than a Quadrillion Tokens a Year

stories.headline: Logistics startup Stord raises $250M at $3B valuation, doubling its worth

key_facts.fact: E-commerce logistics company Stord raised a $250 million round at a $3 billion valuation, announced Tuesday May 26, doubling its valuation from a year-ago round
key_facts.excerpt: E-commerce logistics company Stord has raised a $250 million round at a $3 billion valuation, it announced Tuesday. This doubles its valuation from a year-ago round.

key_facts.fact: The funding was led by Strike Capital with participation from Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Franklin Templeton, Baillie Gifford, G Squared and Bond
key_facts.excerpt: The new funding was led by Strike Capital with participation from Kleiner Perkins, Founders Fund, Franklin Templeton, Baillie Gifford, G Squared, and Bond.

key_facts.fact: In 2025 Stord raised a $200 million mega-round, also led by Strike Capital, that valued it at $1.5 billion; it has now raised a total of about $775 million to date
key_facts.excerpt: in 2025 raised a $200 million mega-round, also led by Strike Capital, that brought it to a $1.5 billion valuation. It has now raised a total of about $775 million to date.

key_facts.fact: Stord positions itself as a competitor to Amazon's fulfillment operations
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon fulfillment competitor Stord raises $250M at $3B valuation.

stories.headline: French preventive-health startup Lucis raises $20M Series A led by Singular, four months after seed

key_facts.fact: Paris-based preventive health platform Lucis, which uses blood biomarker analysis and AI, raised a $20 million (about €17.1 million) Series A announced May 26, led by Singular with participation from General Catalyst and Y Combinator
key_facts.excerpt: Preventive health platform Lucis has raised $20 million Series A, led by Singular, with participation from General Catalyst, Y Combinator, and angels including investors behind Runna, Céline Lazorthes (Resilience), and Manu Lecomte.

key_facts.fact: The round comes just four months after Lucis's $8 million (€7.2 million) seed in December 2025, bringing total funding to about $28 million in its first year
key_facts.excerpt: The round follows Lucis's $8 million seed raised four months ago, bringing total funding to $28 million.

key_facts.fact: Founded in 2025 by Maxime Berthelot and Baptiste Debever and a Y Combinator 2025 graduate, Lucis maps a roughly 110-biomarker blood panel against a user's medical history via an AI companion app
key_facts.excerpt: Founded last year by Maxime Berthelot and Baptiste Debever, Lucis uses an AI companion app to map a 110-biomarker blood panel against a user's medical history.

key_facts.fact: Lucis has grown to more than 10,000 users across France, the UK, Ireland and Portugal and delivered over one million biomarker tests, with 75% of users improving key health markers within six months; it plans to expand into Spain, Germany and Italy by end-2026
key_facts.excerpt: Lucis has 10,000 users, 1M+ biomarker tests run, and 75% of users improving key health markers within six months, without medication... Spain, Germany, and Italy are targeted by the end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: The deal is Singular's first big preventive-health investment; the firm built its reputation backing Algolia, Qonto and Stripe and has raised over €625 million across two funds
key_facts.excerpt: The VC firm behind Algolia, Qonto and Stripe has never led a preventive health deal until now, backing Paris-based Lucis with a $20M Series A... the firm... has raised over €625M across two funds.
